bull_bear.body: Board approved buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at INR 1,600/share, funded by existing cash (INR 600cr); management cites undervaluation relative to earnings power. No major M&A announced; focus on organic scaling.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Transition costs and headcount slowdown in FY27 due to new Labor Codes implementation; geopolitical energy price inflation impacting client sentiment; concentration risk in BFSI sector despite diversification; potential regulatory notices (PF/GST) though management expresses high confidence in legal defense.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; new CEO Suparna Mitra emphasizes 'profitable growth' and 'operating leverage' over blunt volume; transparent about one-off headcount impacts but bullish on structural margin expansion and formalization trends.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'underlying' business actually grew headcount by 14k in FY26 despite reported decline, masking the strength of the core engine; 24% of Q4 gross joinees were first-time formal employees, highlighting the company's role in India's informal-to-formal labor shift which is underappreciated in pure revenue metrics.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Completed a ₹238 Cr buyback (14.87 lakh shares at ₹1,600/share) in July 2026."
- "Net free cash of ₹350 Cr as of quarter-end, aided by a ₹38 Cr income-tax refund including interest of Rs.8.2cr."
- "TDS receivable outstanding of ~₹145 Cr; DSO in staffing at 6 days, funding exposure 16%."
- "Divestment of 30% stake in Crystal HR on account of portfolio rationalisation" - described as portfolio rationalisation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strong market position: established brand equity and a leading position in the temporary staffing industry
- Experience of promoters in the staffing sector strengthens strategic direction and execution
- Reputed and diverse customer base across consumer durables, FMCG, BFSI, IT services, e-commerce and telecom
- Reduced customer concentration - revenue contribution from the top 20 clients cut to around 37% during H1 FY2026 from approximately 45% in FY2025
- Financially well positioned - low leverage, strong capitalisation and coverage ratios and healthy liquidity, with free cash reserves exceeding Rs 300 Crores
- ISO 27001-certified integrated IT platform supporting 3.5 lakh associates and apprentices, with benefit plans that help manage attrition
- Scale of delivery network - 7,500+ locations across 28 states and 25 lakh+ people hired till date
- Partnerships with over 100 GCCs and collaboration with over 20 universities for education-integrated apprenticeship programmes
- Compliance capability positions the Company as a reliable outsourcing partner within India's complex regulatory environment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Labour law and regulatory compliance risk — Regulatory non-compliance could result in penalties, litigation, business disruption and reputational impact; management flags that regulatory developments may affect headcount levels and operational flexibility, as observed during Q3, and that net apprenticeships in the Degree Apprenticeship segment declined by 2,400 in FY26 primarily due to regulatory-led transitions by large clients. Mitigated through technology-enabled compliance monitoring, regulatory tracking, audits and employee training.
- Structurally low margins and high attrition in general staffing — The Company's own SWOT lists inherent narrow margins as a weakness: the general staffing segment is characterised by structurally low margins and high attrition levels, so profitability is sensitive to mix and to hiring in non-metro regions where average salary levels are considerably lower than in urban areas.
- Pricing and profitability risk from wage inflation — Wage inflation and pricing pressures may affect margins and financial performance; mitigation is through pricing reviews, productivity initiatives and cost optimisation measures. Operating margins are also impacted by annual employee cost increments.
- Talent retention risk — Attrition of skilled professionals may affect service delivery, client engagement and organisational performance; mitigated through career development programmes, internal mobility, leadership development and succession planning.
- Market adaptability - IT sector headwinds and demand cyclicality — Changes in hiring activity and workforce demand may affect growth and profitability; management specifically flags that continued weakness in the IT sector may affect hiring demand within the specialised staffing segment, where hiring demand remained measured and focused on niche, high-skill roles. Mitigation is via market intelligence, sector diversification and strategic reviews.
- Cybersecurity and data protection — Cyber incidents may affect employee, client and business data with operational and reputational consequences - material for a business whose ISO 27001-certified integrated IT platform supports 3.5 lakh associates and apprentices. Mitigated by information security controls, cybersecurity assessments, access management and incident response plans.
- M&A integration risk — Integration challenges may affect operational performance and expected synergies; relevant given recent acquisitions including TSR and Wallet in the HRTech segment. Mitigation is through structured integration roadmaps, dedicated integration teams and governance oversight.
- Client concentration and seasonality of the EdTech segment — Revenue contribution from the top 20 clients was reduced to around 37% during H1 FY2026 from approximately 45% in FY2025, so concentration remains material even after improved diversification; separately, operating margins are impacted by the seasonal nature of the EdTech segment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: General Staffing: 2.87 lakh associates (Q4), PAPM INR 689 (+20pts vs Q1); underlying business added 14k associates excluding in-sourcing. Specialised Staffing: 7,500 associates; GCC contributes 67% of segment revenue; Global business revenue +200% YoY. Degree Apprenticeship: +1,000 net adds in Q4; strong momentum in GCC/Manufacturing. HR Services: Full year EBITDA +22% YoY; Q4 seasonality impacted by EdTech billing timing.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "TeamLease has established itself as an end-to-end people supply chain solutions provider, delivering integrated workforce solutions across the employee lifecycle", spanning "manpower sourcing, talent acquisition, workforce digitization, productivity enhancement, and compliance management" across the 3Es: Employment, Employability and E-workforce.
- The deck frames the four Labour Codes as the "most consequential regulatory shift for organized staffing in a generation" and reads it both ways: a structural positive because "a single central licence, uniform wage definitions, and mandatory formal appointment letters raise the compliance bar in a way that favours large, organized players like TeamLease over unorganized contractors", the core "formalization" thesis; but a "near-term cost/complexity" because "the 50%-of-CTC wage definition raises PF/gratuity cost per associate and requires payroll-system and contract rework across the client base".
- Scale claims: "4,000+ Employers served across the group", "26 Lakh+ People placed to date", "3.4 Lakh+ Associates & trainees", "7.5 Lakh+ Students", "28 States" and "7,500+ locations"; the journey slide describes "25 years from a four-office start-up to India's largest private-sector employer ambition" and notes that in 2021 it "Became India's largest IT staffing company by headcount".
- GCCs are called "the single largest driver of incremental staffing demand in India", with "67% of specialised staffing revenue originated from GCCs" and specialised staffing "the segment best positioned to capture GCC and technical-role demand".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership] "2026 ₹238 Cr buyback completed; new MD & CEO (Suparna Mitra) takes charge"; the board slide lists Ms. Suparna Mitra as Managing Director & CEO, Ashok Reddy as Executive Vice Chairman & Whole-Time Director, Narayan Ramachandran as Chairman & Non-Executive Non-Independent Director and Manish Sabharwal as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director.
- [Regulation] Labour Codes timeline: "21 Nov 2025 All four Labour Codes (Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, OSH) notified as law, replacing 29 earlier central statutes"; "8 May 2026 Ministry of Labour & Employment notifies the Central Rules under all four Codes"; state rules "Vary by state, some finalized, others still in draft"; and ongoing "single central OSH licence for staffing firms replaces state-by-state registration".
- [Risk] "Watch-item: GCC linked demand is more discretionary to global technology capex cycles than blue-collar general staffing, a slowdown in global IT/tech spend is the main risk to this vector."
- [Corporate] Listed on BSE and NSE in 2016 (BSE: 539658 | NSE: TEAMLEASE | ISIN: INE985S01024); founded 2000; first PE investment from Gaja Capital in 2011-16.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Since its inception in 2002, TeamLease has built integrated workforce solutions spanning manpower sourcing, talent acquisition, workforce digitisation, productivity enhancement and compliance management. Its activities span workforce deployment, work-integrated learning, specialised hiring and workforce management solutions, organised around the 3Es of Employment, Employability and E-workforce. Clients range across consumer durables, FMCG, BFSI, IT services, e-commerce and telecom, and include over 100 Global Capability Centres.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **General Staffing:** Large-scale workforce deployment, Associate services including earned wage access, loan offerings and a health and medical benefits category
- **Specialised Staffing:** Niche and digital talent solutions, Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) structures, Recruitment process outsourcing and managed services
- **Degree Apprenticeship:** Industry-aligned apprenticeship programmes, Work-integrated learning (WILP), Learning-integrated apprenticeship model
- **Hiring and Recruitment:** HireTech (AI-based search engine), freshersworld.com
- **Regulatory Compliances:** Labour and corporate law compliance outsourcing
- **HRTech Services:** Wallet HR, TSR
- **Learning Services:** Upskilling and reskilling programmes, LMS learning journeys

latest_quarter.body: PAPM improved to INR 689 (Q4) from INR 669 (Q1) driven by 70% new mandates on variable markup model and shift to mid-sized/higher-margin logos. Cost-to-hire reduced structurally by 20% YoY via tech/AI efficiencies and sourcing variabilization.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Recovery expected in H1 FY27 post planned exit of 10k low-margin headcount. Margin: Targeting >20% YoY EBITDA growth in FY27 driven by mix shift to Specialised/DA and operating leverage. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline with 20k open roles; focus on variable markup models. Capex/Commissioning: Low capex intensity; focus on tech/AI integration rather than heavy infrastructure.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ~20,000 open positions at start of FY27; recovered 70% of volume loss and 80% of recurring revenue loss from NBFC in-sourcing by year-end.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scaling GCC 'bot' models and RPO for higher realization; AI-led hiring tools productizing proprietary data; expansion of PMIS 3.0 internship scheme; formalization tailwind from new Labor Codes shifting share from unorganized to organized players.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deliver profitable and sustainable growth while improving operating leverage - stated as the clear forward priority alongside strengthening higher-value businesses, investing in technology and talent, and deepening client relationships.
- Grow the higher-margin segments faster than General Staffing: Specialised Staffing and HR Services both operate at margins above General Staffing, and consolidated margin is said to depend more on these segments compounding.
- Shift General Staffing contracting to variable markup and outcome-linked structures - close to 70% of new mandates are now signed on variable markup rather than a fixed fee, so margin moves with client volumes.
- Lower cost-to-hire through process and technology rather than pricing, and invest in compliance, payroll and associate-engagement platforms so a larger associate base can be serviced without adding core headcount in proportion.
- Build specialist recruitment capability and technology for GCC and niche mandates, which management says are won on capability rather than price.
- Expand GCC engagement models - Build-Operate-Transfer, staffing solutions, recruitment process outsourcing and managed services - with the GCC book now about 60% of Specialised Staffing associates and 67% of its revenue.
- Deploy technology as a central plank of long-term strategy: greater automation, platform modernisation, AI applied across selected business processes, and continued investment in HireTech.
- Strengthen the HR Services portfolio through technology-enabled solutions, regulatory compliance and the integration of Wallet HR.
- Capital allocation order of priority: fund organic growth and technology first, pursue M&A outreach for opportunities in the higher-margin businesses, then return what is genuinely surplus to shareholders.
- Exit mandates where the economics no longer work - planned exits continue in Q1 and Q2 of FY27 across General Staffing and Degree Apprenticeship, described as the Company's own decision.
- Long-term ambition to become the largest private sector employer in India and the largest staffing company in the world by headcount.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TeamLease is an asset-light services business, so expansion is described as footprint, platform and portfolio build-out rather than plant capacity. The Company reports 7,500+ locations across 28 states and 16 offices - 14 domestic (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar, Chennai, Dehradun, Delhi, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Pune, Noida, Vadodara) and two international (Singapore and Dubai) - with reach expanding through deeper penetration in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets and a growing international footprint. Growth has historically been inorganic as well as organic: the corporate journey records the acquisition of ASAP Info Systems and Nichepro Technologies (2015-16), Keystone Business Solutions, a 30% stake in FW.com, Evolve Technologies, a 40% stake in Schoolguru, a 33.33% stake in Avantis RegTech, the IT staffing business of Ecentric and IMSI, the increase of FW.com to 100% and Avantis to 60%, entry into the Singapore and UAE markets, and a 90% stake in TSR Darashaw HR Services. Forward expansion levers stated are M&A outreach for opportunities in the higher-margin businesses, expanded Build-Operate-Transfer engagements within Specialised Staffing, an accelerated shift towards higher-value skills (data analytics, cybersecurity, digital transformation and AI-related roles), and continued platform investment that lets the Company carry a larger associate book without adding core staff proportionately. The Board's Report notes that the Company is closely watching market conditions, is evaluating all projects in pipeline and will pace them in line with market conditions, with revised timelines for the development plan to be re-assessed as the situation unfolds and only minimal capital spends foreseen against the development pipeline for the year. No rupee capex quantum is usable: the named-disclosure blocks for Capital commitments and Segment capital expenditure arrived with no attributable period and no printed unit.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continued formalisation of the economy, expanding Global Capability Centres, rapid digital adoption and growing demand for specialised skills are reshaping the employment landscape and are the structural opportunities the Company expects to participate in.
- Demand composition rather than demand level is changing under generative AI: growth is clearly in AI-adjacent skills - cloud, data security and governance, and integration roles - while AI has impacted entry-level coding and testing jobs.
- Employers are paying premiums of 30% to 40% for cybersecurity talent with AI exposure; the Company placed 500 to 600 mid and senior AI-talent people over the last two quarters at better than average realisations, and describes its constraint as just-in-time supply, not demand.
- Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: EBITDA grew 14% on revenue growth of 6%, with cost-to-hire reduced by about 20% during the year and a larger share of sourcing spend moved to a variable structure.
- PAPM (realisation per associate per month) in General Staffing improved from Rs 665 at the close of FY25 to Rs 689 in the fourth quarter, converting into margin through platform investment.
- General Staffing is a scale business with a pass-through cost structure, so margin moves in basis points rather than steps and will remain a sub-2% EBITDA margin business.
- FY26 headcount and revenue were impacted by a single transaction - one large NBFC client moved approximately 25,000 associates/trainees onto its own payroll in Q3 following a regulatory directive; excluding it, about 14,000 associates were added during FY26.
- FY26 PBT includes a Rs 26.79 crore income-tax refund relating to previous assessment years; adjusted for one-offs, underlying PBT growth is about 20% YoY.
- India's staffing industry in FY26 is characterised by rapid formalisation and a transition toward high-skill flexi-staffing models, supported by GCC expansion, a resurgent manufacturing sector and hiring moving into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
- The Indian flexi staffing industry is projected to grow by 12.6% over the next two financial years, reaching 9.6 million by FY27, with e-commerce the primary growth driver alongside retail and hospitality.
- Policy tailwinds: the new labour code consolidates fragmented regulations and encourages companies to engage organised staffing providers, while GST reforms enable seamless interstate operations.
- Degree Apprenticeship demand is supported by increasing industry adoption, NAPS/NATS policy support for work-integrated learning and growing enterprise focus on compliance.
- Indian macro backdrop cited as supportive: 7.7% GDP growth during the fiscal year, historically low inflation, RBI rate cuts of 100 basis points to 5.25%, and Union Budget FY 2026-27 capital expenditure up 11.5% to Rs 12.22 lakh crore.
- The Company entered the year with roughly 23,000 open positions, 15% to 20% higher than the preceding quarter.
- Demand-side constraint in specialised AI/cybersecurity talent is described as just-in-time supply rather than demand.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: TeamLease delivered resilient profit growth (PAT +22% YoY) despite a significant revenue drag from a single NBFC client in-sourcing 20k associates, proving the efficacy of its operating leverage and cost-to-hire reduction strategies. The approved INR buyback and strong cash position (INR 600cr) signal capital discipline, while the strategic pivot toward high-margin GCC, AI-skills, and apprenticeship models positions the firm to capture India's workforce formalization tailwinds in FY27.

currentContext.expansion: TeamLease is an asset-light services business, so expansion is described as footprint, platform and portfolio build-out rather than plant capacity. The Company reports 7,500+ locations across 28 states and 16 offices - 14 domestic (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar, Chennai, Dehradun, Delhi, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Pune, Noida, Vadodara) and two international (Singapore and Dubai) - with reach expanding through deeper penetration in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets and a growing international footprint. Growth has historically been inorganic as well as organic: the corporate journey records the acquisition of ASAP Info Systems and Nichepro Technologies (2015-16), Keystone Business Solutions, a 30% stake in FW.com, Evolve Technologies, a 40% stake in Schoolguru, a 33.33% stake in Avantis RegTech, the IT staffing business of Ecentric and IMSI, the increase of FW.com to 100% and Avantis to 60%, entry into the Singapore and UAE markets, and a 90% stake in TSR Darashaw HR Services. Forward expansion levers stated are M&A outreach for opportunities in the higher-margin businesses, expanded Build-Operate-Transfer engagements within Specialised Staffing, an accelerated shift towards higher-value skills (data analytics, cybersecurity, digital transformation and AI-related roles), and continued platform investment that lets the Company carry a larger associate book without adding core staff proportionately. The Board's Report notes that the Company is closely watching market conditions, is evaluating all projects in pipeline and will pace them in line with market conditions, with revised timelines for the development plan to be re-assessed as the situation unfolds and only minimal capital spends foreseen against the development pipeline for the year. No rupee capex quantum is usable: the named-disclosure blocks for Capital commitments and Segment capital expenditure arrived with no attributable period and no printed unit.

risks.risk: Labour law and regulatory compliance risk
risks.note: Regulatory non-compliance could result in penalties, litigation, business disruption and reputational impact; management flags that regulatory developments may affect headcount levels and operational flexibility, as observed during Q3, and that net apprenticeships in the Degree Apprenticeship segment declined by 2,400 in FY26 primarily due to regulatory-led transitions by large clients. Mitigated through technology-enabled compliance monitoring, regulatory tracking, audits and employee training.

risks.risk: Structurally low margins and high attrition in general staffing
risks.note: The Company's own SWOT lists inherent narrow margins as a weakness: the general staffing segment is characterised by structurally low margins and high attrition levels, so profitability is sensitive to mix and to hiring in non-metro regions where average salary levels are considerably lower than in urban areas.

risks.risk: Pricing and profitability risk from wage inflation
risks.note: Wage inflation and pricing pressures may affect margins and financial performance; mitigation is through pricing reviews, productivity initiatives and cost optimisation measures. Operating margins are also impacted by annual employee cost increments.

Attrition of skilled professionals may affect service delivery, client engagement and organisational performance; mitigated through career development programmes, internal mobility, leadership development and succession planning.

risks.risk: Market adaptability - IT sector headwinds and demand cyclicality
risks.note: Changes in hiring activity and workforce demand may affect growth and profitability; management specifically flags that continued weakness in the IT sector may affect hiring demand within the specialised staffing segment, where hiring demand remained measured and focused on niche, high-skill roles. Mitigation is via market intelligence, sector diversification and strategic reviews.

Cyber incidents may affect employee, client and business data with operational and reputational consequences - material for a business whose ISO 27001-certified integrated IT platform supports 3.5 lakh associates and apprentices. Mitigated by information security controls, cybersecurity assessments, access management and incident response plans.

Integration challenges may affect operational performance and expected synergies; relevant given recent acquisitions including TSR and Wallet in the HRTech segment. Mitigation is through structured integration roadmaps, dedicated integration teams and governance oversight.

risks.risk: Client concentration and seasonality of the EdTech segment
risks.note: Revenue contribution from the top 20 clients was reduced to around 37% during H1 FY2026 from approximately 45% in FY2025, so concentration remains material even after improved diversification; separately, operating margins are impacted by the seasonal nature of the EdTech segment.

one-line thesis: TeamLease delivered resilient profit growth (PAT +22% YoY) despite a significant revenue drag from a single NBFC client in-sourcing 20k associates, proving the efficacy of its operating leverage and cost-to-hire reduction strategies. The approved INR buyback and strong cash position (INR 600cr) signal capital discipline, while the strategic pivot toward high-margin GCC, AI-skills, and apprenticeship models positions the firm to capture India's workforce formalization tailwinds in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,925cr (Q4, -2% QoQ due to NBFC in-sourcing); Full Year +6% YoY. EBITDA Margin: 1.5% (Q4, +10bps QoQ); Full Year 1.34% (+10bps YoY). PAT: +22% YoY (Q4), +33% YoY (FY26); includes INR 143cr tax refund one-off (underlying PBT +20% YoY). Order Book: ~20k open positions at FY27 start (+15-20% QoQ). Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash INR 600cr); One-offs include INR 143cr tax refund and INR 5.82cr provision for labor court exceptional item.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Recovery expected in H1 FY27 post planned exit of 10k low-margin headcount. growth verticals / optionality: Scaling GCC 'bot' models and RPO for higher realization; AI-led hiring tools productizing proprietary data; expansion of PMIS 3.0 internship scheme; formalization tailwind from new Labor Codes shifting share from unorganized to organized players.
margins & cost dynamics: PAPM improved to INR 689 (Q4) from INR 669 (Q1) driven by 70% new mandates on variable markup model and shift to mid-sized/higher-margin logos. Cost-to-hire reduced structurally by 20% YoY via tech/AI efficiencies and sourcing variabilization.
capex / expansion: Minimal traditional capex; investments focused on AI-enabled ATS, upskilling recruiters, and backend technology platforms to drive operating leverage without linear headcount increase.

management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; new CEO Suparna Mitra emphasizes 'profitable growth' and 'operating leverage' over blunt volume; transparent about one-off headcount impacts but bullish on structural margin expansion and formalization trends.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'underlying' business actually grew headcount by 14k in FY26 despite reported decline, masking the strength of the core engine; 24% of Q4 gross joinees were first-time formal employees, highlighting the company's role in India's informal-to-formal labor shift which is underappreciated in pure revenue metrics.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued formalisation of the economy, expanding Global Capability Centres, rapid digital adoption and growing demand for specialised skills are reshaping the employment landscape and are the structural opportunities the Company expects to participate in.
- Demand composition rather than demand level is changing under generative AI: growth is clearly in AI-adjacent skills - cloud, data security and governance, and integration roles - while AI has impacted entry-level coding and testing jobs.
- Employers are paying premiums of 30% to 40% for cybersecurity talent with AI exposure; the Company placed 500 to 600 mid and senior AI-talent people over the last two quarters at better than average realisations, and describes its constraint as just-in-time supply, not demand.
- Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: EBITDA grew 14% on revenue growth of 6%, with cost-to-hire reduced by about 20% during the year and a larger share of sourcing spend moved to a variable structure.
- PAPM (realisation per associate per month) in General Staffing improved from Rs 665 at the close of FY25 to Rs 689 in the fourth quarter, converting into margin through platform investment.
- General Staffing is a scale business with a pass-through cost structure, so margin moves in basis points rather than steps and will remain a sub-2% EBITDA margin business.
- FY26 headcount and revenue were impacted by a single transaction - one large NBFC client moved approximately 25,000 associates/trainees onto its own payroll in Q3 following a regulatory directive; excluding it, about 14,000 associates were added during FY26.
- FY26 PBT includes a Rs 26.79 crore income-tax refund relating to previous assessment years; adjusted for one-offs, underlying PBT growth is about 20% YoY.
- India's staffing industry in FY26 is characterised by rapid formalisation and a transition toward high-skill flexi-staffing models, supported by GCC expansion, a resurgent manufacturing sector and hiring moving into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
- The Indian flexi staffing industry is projected to grow by 12.6% over the next two financial years, reaching 9.6 million by FY27, with e-commerce the primary growth driver alongside retail and hospitality.
- Policy tailwinds: the new labour code consolidates fragmented regulations and encourages companies to engage organised staffing providers, while GST reforms enable seamless interstate operations.
- Degree Apprenticeship demand is supported by increasing industry adoption, NAPS/NATS policy support for work-integrated learning and growing enterprise focus on compliance.
- Indian macro backdrop cited as supportive: 7.7% GDP growth during the fiscal year, historically low inflation, RBI rate cuts of 100 basis points to 5.25%, and Union Budget FY 2026-27 capital expenditure up 11.5% to Rs 12.22 lakh crore.
- The Company entered the year with roughly 23,000 open positions, 15% to 20% higher than the preceding quarter.
- Demand-side constraint in specialised AI/cybersecurity talent is described as just-in-time supply rather than demand.

margins.body: PAPM improved to INR 689 (Q4) from INR 669 (Q1) driven by 70% new mandates on variable markup model and shift to mid-sized/higher-margin logos. Cost-to-hire reduced structurally by 20% YoY via tech/AI efficiencies and sourcing variabilization.

The Board's Report notes that the Company is closely watching market conditions, is evaluating all projects in pipeline and will pace them in line with market conditions, with revised timelines for the development plan to be re-assessed as the situation unfolds and only minimal capital spends foreseen against the development pipeline for the year. management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and disciplined; new CEO Suparna Mitra emphasizes 'profitable growth' and 'operating leverage' over blunt volume; transparent about one-off headcount impacts but bullish on structural margin expansion and formalization trends.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong market position: established brand equity and a leading position in the temporary staffing industry
- Experience of promoters in the staffing sector strengthens strategic direction and execution
- Reputed and diverse customer base across consumer durables, FMCG, BFSI, IT services, e-commerce and telecom
- Reduced customer concentration - revenue contribution from the top 20 clients cut to around 37% during H1 FY2026 from approximately 45% in FY2025
- Financially well positioned - low leverage, strong capitalisation and coverage ratios and healthy liquidity, with free cash reserves exceeding Rs 300 Crores
- ISO 27001-certified integrated IT platform supporting 3.5 lakh associates and apprentices, with benefit plans that help manage attrition
- Scale of delivery network - 7,500+ locations across 28 states and 25 lakh+ people hired till date
- Partnerships with over 100 GCCs and collaboration with over 20 universities for education-integrated apprenticeship programmes
- Compliance capability positions the Company as a reliable outsourcing partner within India's complex regulatory environment

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Transition costs and headcount slowdown in FY27 due to new Labor Codes implementation; geopolitical energy price inflation impacting client sentiment; concentration risk in BFSI sector despite diversification; potential regulatory notices (PF/GST) though management expresses high confidence in legal defense.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'underlying' business actually grew headcount by 14k in FY26 despite reported decline, masking the strength of the core engine; 24% of Q4 gross joinees were first-time formal employees, highlighting the company's role in India's informal-to-formal labor shift which is underappreciated in pure revenue metrics.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deliver profitable and sustainable growth while improving operating leverage - stated as the clear forward priority alongside strengthening higher-value businesses, investing in technology and talent, and deepening client relationships.
- Grow the higher-margin segments faster than General Staffing: Specialised Staffing and HR Services both operate at margins above General Staffing, and consolidated margin is said to depend more on these segments compounding.
- Shift General Staffing contracting to variable markup and outcome-linked structures - close to 70% of new mandates are now signed on …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Labor Codes increasing compliance burden for unorganized competitors | TeamLease Services Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management explicitly states 90% of industry is unorganized; new codes and Shram Suvidha Portal will force formalization, driving market share to compliant players like TeamLease. |
| NBFC in-sourcing reduced reported headcount | TeamLease Services Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Recovery of 80% of recurring revenue and 20k open roles suggests the in-sourcing was a one-off event, not a structural loss of client trust, setting up a low-base rebound in FY27. |
| Traditional IT hiring freeze | Generic IT Staffing Peers | loser | Med | Shift in demand is strictly toward AI/Cloud/Cybersecurity skills; peers lacking specialized GCC/AI capabilities may face margin compression while TeamLease pivots successfully. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership] "2026 ₹238 Cr buyback completed; new MD & CEO (Suparna Mitra) takes charge"; the board slide lists Ms. Suparna Mitra as Managing Director & CEO, Ashok Reddy as Executive Vice Chairman & Whole-Time Director, Narayan Ramachandran as Chairman & Non-Executive Non-Independent Director and Manish Sabharwal as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director.
- [Regulation] Labour Codes timeline: "21 Nov 2025 All four Labour Codes (Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, OSH) notified as law, replacing 29 earlier central statutes"; "8 May 2026 Ministry of Labour & Employment notifies the Central Rules under all four Codes"; state rules "Vary by state, some finalized, others still in draft"; and ongoing "single central OSH licence for staffing firms replaces state-by-state registration".
- [Risk] "Watch-item: GCC linked demand is more discretionary to global technology capex cycles than blue-collar general staffing, a slowdown in global IT/tech spend is the main risk to this vector."
- [Corporate] Listed on BSE and NSE in 2016 (BSE: 539658 | NSE: TEAMLEASE | ISIN: INE985S01024); founded 2000; first PE investment from Gaja Capital in 2011-16.

one-line thesis: TeamLease delivered resilient profit growth (PAT +22% YoY) despite a significant revenue drag from a single NBFC client in-sourcing 20k associates, proving the efficacy of its operating leverage and cost-to-hire reduction strategies. The approved INR buyback and strong cash position (INR 600cr) signal capital discipline, while the strategic pivot toward high-margin GCC, AI-skills, and apprenticeship models positions the firm to capture India's workforce formalization tailwinds in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,925cr (Q4, -2% QoQ due to NBFC in-sourcing); Full Year +6% YoY. EBITDA Margin: 1.5% (Q4, +10bps QoQ); Full Year 1.34% (+10bps YoY). PAT: +22% YoY (Q4), +33% YoY (FY26); includes INR 143cr tax refund one-off (underlying PBT +20% YoY). Order Book: ~20k open positions at FY27 start (+15-20% QoQ). Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash INR 600cr); One-offs include INR 143cr tax refund and INR 5.82cr provision for labor court exceptional item.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Recovery expected in H1 FY27 post planned exit of 10k low-margin headcount. Margin: Targeting >20% YoY EBITDA growth in FY27 driven by mix shift to Specialised/DA and operating leverage. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline with 20k open roles; focus on variable markup models. Capex/Commissioning: Low capex intensity; focus on tech/AI integration rather than heavy infrastructure.
order book & pipeline: ~20,000 open positions at start of FY27; recovered 70% of volume loss and 80% of recurring revenue loss from NBFC in-sourcing by year-end.
segment / subsidiary detail: General Staffing: 2.87 lakh associates (Q4), PAPM INR 689 (+20pts vs Q1); underlying business added 14k associates excluding in-sourcing. Specialised Staffing: 7,500 associates; GCC contributes 67% of segment revenue; Global business revenue +200% YoY. Degree Apprenticeship: +1,000 net adds in Q4; strong momentum in GCC/Manufacturing. HR Services: Full year EBITDA +22% YoY; Q4 seasonality impacted by EdTech billing timing.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling GCC 'bot' models and RPO for higher realization; AI-led hiring tools productizing proprietary data; expansion of PMIS 3.0 internship scheme; formalization tailwind from new Labor Codes shifting share from unorganized to organized players.
margins & cost dynamics: PAPM improved to INR 689 (Q4) from INR 669 (Q1) driven by 70% new mandates on variable markup model and shift to mid-sized/higher-margin logos. Cost-to-hire reduced structurally by 20% YoY via tech/AI efficiencies and sourcing variabilization.
capex / expansion: Minimal traditional capex; investments focused on AI-enabled ATS, upskilling recruiters, and backend technology platforms to drive operating leverage without linear headcount increase.
capital allocation: Board approved buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at INR 1,600/share, funded by existing cash (INR 600cr); management cites undervaluation relative to earnings power. No major M&A announced; focus on organic scaling.

themes.title: Workforce solutions & facility management formalization
themes.need: Formalization, GCC hiring and compliance outsourcing drive staffing and integrated facility-management demand - QUESS/TEAMLEASE on flexi-staffing & GCC enablement; SIS/KRYSTAL/UDS on integrated security + facility management. Headcount additions and wage-bill growth are the near-term levers.
